content: Children diagnosed with type 1 diabetes are at an increased risk of developing other autoimmune conditions, including thyroid dysfunction. It is recommended to test for thyroid antibodies, specifically antithyroid peroxidase and antithyroglobulin antibodies, at the time of diagnosis. If these antibodies are present, periodic re-evaluation is advised. Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels should be assessed at diagnosis or shortly thereafter, particularly in cases where maintaining stable blood glucose levels is difficult. If the initial TSH levels are normal, it is recommended to re-check TSH every 1 to 2 years, or sooner if the child exhibits symptoms of thyroid dysfunction or has a family history of thyroid disease. Thyroid dysfunction, such as hypothyroidism, can negatively affect growth and metabolic control in children with type 1 diabetes, making early detection and management critical.
